name: Chiang Ching-kuo
role: Republic of China premier (1972–1978) and president (1978–1988)
summary: Chiang combined Chinese nationalist anti-communism with state-led industrial development. After a career deeply involved in authoritarian repression, he initiated a qualified opening to opposition parties and a freer press, and rejected family and military succession.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Favored government-led allocation, despite accepting some price and trade liberalization.

public-ownership.rationale: Resisted privatization and treated major public enterprises as collective assets; later accepted possible bank privatization with safeguards.

gradual-change.rationale: Pursued staged institutional reform and cautioned against rash responses to changing conditions.

free-trade.rationale: Eventually directed trade opening, while retaining reservations about liberalization.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Personally promoted nuclear power within the Ten Major Construction Projects.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Protected domestic industry, then authorized qualified trade liberalization under US pressure.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Personally directed strategic steel, shipbuilding and semiconductor investment.

one-party-rule.rationale: Ultimately authorized opposition parties, reversing his earlier enforcement of KMT monopoly.

democracy-best.rationale: His mature speeches endorsed constitutional democracy and he initiated political opening; full electoral equality remained incomplete.

right-to-secede.rationale: His political opening required rejection of separatism.

equal-outcomes.rationale: His final address sought equality of wealth, alongside prosperity.

limit-population.rationale: Personally instructed officials to reduce population growth and revive stalled reproductive legislation.

direct-action.rationale: Sought political opening through constitutional and electoral reform.

national-mission.rationale: Presented Taiwan’s democratization as a model the mainland Chinese should emulate.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Reportedly ordered an investigation of the Lieyu massacre and accepted responsibility for addressing Henry Liu’s murder; this falls short of comprehensive accountability.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Conditioned legal political organization on constitutional loyalty and anti-communism.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Ended Taiwan’s martial law in 1987 after defending it for decades, while retaining national-security restrictions.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Froze necessities, then admitted price-control errors and accepted cost-reflective oil prices; the later food-price principle remains unclear.

party-controls-media.rationale: Personally ended newspaper-number and page-limit restrictions in January 1988, reversing earlier censorship.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Explicitly affirmed continuing alignment with the United States.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Presided over a clandestine weapons-capability effort while denying any intention to build nuclear arms; the public and operational records conflict.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Rejected Beijing’s proposed accommodation as a route to communist control.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: His mature speeches committed government to constitutional rules and law.

elective-rulers.rationale: On the same occasion he said the next president would be elected as the Constitution stipulates, not inherit from him; the president was then chosen by the National Assembly, not by the public.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Financed major development projects with foreign loans.

military-guardian-role.rationale: In the same speech explicitly rejected future military rule.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Regarded excessive consumption as wasteful and damaging to savings and development.

defeat-communism.rationale: Explicitly committed to defeating communist rule and refused negotiations with the CCP.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Tolerated the DPP in 1986 after decades of repression; retained anti-communist and anti-separatist restrictions.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Said Taiwan would remain aligned with the United States.

dynastic-succession.rationale: In December 1985 explicitly ruled out his family as presidential successors.

capital-controls.rationale: Ultimately permitted foreign-exchange deregulation in 1987 after prolonged controls.

close-ties-china.rationale: Retained no official contact, negotiation or compromise even while permitting family visits.

notes:
Whole-career review includes Soviet and Gannan years, Shanghai price controls, Taiwan security leadership, state-led development and final reforms. Mature reforms take precedence over earlier one-party repression; security restrictions survived the lifting of martial law, which did not extend to every offshore island. Economic liberalization was partial and accompanied by reservations, so it is not treated as blanket laissez-faire. His 1981 reunification aim does not answer the specific statement about a border drawn by an outside power. Family visits do not establish open borders or diaspora citizenship. Henry Liu’s assassination and the Lieyu massacre were reviewed; no personal order to murder is imputed without evidence, and the latter article carries reliability notices. Nuclear weapons capability remained contested against official assurances; Taiwan had no deployed independent nuclear arsenal. Population legislation was personally prompted, but neither general reproductive autonomy nor every provision of the final law is attributed to him. Culture, religion, minority-language, ecology, technology, labor and remaining null statements were checked against the evidence; party doctrine, relatives’ beliefs, general government practice and ceremonial assent do not fill gaps. No inferred answers.

claude-sonnet-5-5 notes: Independent second pass. Read: both inaugural addresses (1978, 1984), his will, the 1987 martial-law order, Taiwan Communique on the 1986 Graham interview and the draft security law, a CRS report and a 1985 news report. Government and world themes were searched; his economic, society, ecology and technology positions were not found in these texts, and the Ten Projects, population policy and nuclear questions were left to the first audit (not copied). Answers resting on what his government did rather than on his own words are low: Kaohsiung detentions, martial law, the 1987 security law. Not opened: see Blocked (CommonWealth, UPI, Medium mirror: Cloudflare block). The Time August 1985 interview and the 25 December 1985 Chinese text were not reached; the succession answer rests on a news report.
